title: Subscriptions Basics
description: Understand GraphQL subscriptions and how they enable real-time data updates in Apollo Client.

data.text: **GraphQL subscriptions** enable real-time updates from server to client. Unlike queries and mutations, which follow a request-response cycle, subscriptions maintain a persistent connection that pushes data whenever specific events occur on the server.

Subscriptions are one of the three core GraphQL operation types, alongside queries and mutations. They are designed for use cases where the server needs to notify the client about events as they happen, such as new chat messages, live stock prices, or status updates.

items: Use WebSockets or SSE for persistent bidirectional communication
Server pushes data to client only when events occur
Client defines which events it wants to listen for
Connection stays open for the lifetime of the subscription
data.title: Key Characteristics
When to Use Subscriptions
data.text: Use subscriptions when you need immediate updates and the server can detect the event. Use polling only when the server cannot push events, or for very simple integrations.

data.title: GraphQL Subscription Definition

data.text: The syntax looks nearly identical to queries. The only difference is the `subscription` keyword. The server defines which events are available and what data they return.

data.title: useSubscription in a Component
Initial Null Data
data.text: Unlike useQuery, useSubscription starts with null data. The hook fires only when the server pushes an event. Do not treat loading as an error state; it is the normal idle state.

data.caption: How a GraphQL subscription flows from server to client
data.definition:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant W as WebSocket
    participant S as Server
    C->>W: Open WebSocket connection
    W->>S: Connection init + auth
    S-->>W: Connection ack
    C->>W: Subscribe (GQL message)
    W->>S: Forward subscription
    Note over S: Event occurs
    S-->>W: Push data
    W-->>C: onNext(data)
    C->>W: Complete / Unsubscribe
    W->>S: Close frame

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Subscriptions push data from server to client over persistent connections
Syntax mirrors queries but uses the subscription keyword
useSubscription starts with null data and fires on events
WebSockets provide the transport layer for subscriptions
data.takeaway: Subscriptions are the GraphQL-native way to build real-time features.
